steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil. Stir in penne and return to a boil. Cook pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 10 minutes; rinse with cold water and drain well.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, garlic, lemon juice, oregano, salt, and pepper together in a bowl; set aside.
Combine pasta, tomatoes, green and red peppers, onion, cucumber, olives, and feta cheese in a large bowl. Pour vinaigrette over pasta mixture and mix well.
For best flavor, cover salad and chill in the refrigerator before serving to allow flavors to blend. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Greek Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This Greek pasta salad with penne, juicy tomatoes, cucumber, and feta in a tangy dressing has all the refreshing flavors of a classic Greek salad!

video.description: This Greek Pasta Salad recipe makes the perfect dish for summer gatherings. Made with flavorful ingredients and a tangy vinaigrette, it's a refreshing and satisfying salad that everyone will love. Cooked penne pasta is tossed with cherry tomatoes, bell peppers, red onion, cucumber, black olives, and crumbled feta cheese, creating a vibrant medley of colors and textures. The homemade dressing, made with olive oil, red wine vinegar, garlic, lemon juice, and dried oregano, adds a zesty and aromatic touch. Try this Greek Pasta Salad and savor the taste of the Mediterranean!

review.reviewBody: I thought this was the best greek pasta salad I have tried so far. There was exactly the right amount of dressing. You must let it sit for at least 3 hours for the flavors to develop completely. I used grape tomatoes instead of cherry because they taste just fine after being in the fridge and added a smidge more feta cheese. Make sure you add salt and pepper to the dressing as well as the again to the salad after mixing. My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed this one.

I really like the dressing - it's not too strong like some pasta salads. I've made this a number of times, now, and have used roma tomatoes instead of cherry. I added some garbanzo beans. Used fresh oregano. Reduced the olive oil to save fat calories. Traded red wine vinegar for white wine once, and I traded it for tequila lime vinegar another... always fabulous!

What I did was went to the local Grocery store and got the Olives medley from the Olive bar, I used the juice from the olives as well as I used the small balls of Mozzarella. I went to the deli and got 1/4 slices(4) of Provolone cheese, (4) slices of 1/4 Swiss, cut it up using a pizza cutter cause of it being faster. Doing it the way I did I eliminated using any salad dressing, the last thing I put in was shredded Parm cheese. I used the Rainbow pasta.If you want it a little spicy put the small pepperoni in it

Everyone loved this dish! I added artichokes, used mostly white vinegar, and used rotini tri-colored pasta. Super colorful and pretty for summer! I also added a little extra cheese and used a greek olive mix and grape tomatoes. I made this the morning of serving, and poured 1/2 the dressing on then, and the other half at serving.

This is a great pasta salad dressing ! My kids love it! I love that the salad part is so versatile, you can add just about any fresh vegetables or left-over veggies you have on hand, however, do not add add any lettuce/spinach, grated (only), shaved is fine, parmesan cheese, chick peas/garbanzo beans or chicken until ready to serve . The dressing is absolutely fabulous on it's own but can also be modified to fit personal taste, occasion or meal. I.E. white wine vinegar instead of red, amounts to fit your taste: Dill, Basil, Lemon Zest, Honey, Dijon Mustard, Salt & Pepper. Also great as a marinade for chicken, but use red wine vinegar. For pasta you can use any you have on hand from angel hair to ziti, or zoodles, spaghetti squash, orzo, or large pasta shells. This is so easy and can accommodate just about any taste. I'm making a 'mom's cookbook ' for my daughter for when she heads of to college in 2 years and this is a perfect recipe for a novice cook. It is a perfect addition, easy to make, able to use what is on hand, adaptable but will still give her a taste of home. I just hope she doesn't get distracted while cutting up the veggies and cut herself Also, for those whose family say they don't like Feta Cheese, crumble it up in to small bits, don't mention it's in there (unless of course they have an allergy) and guarantee they will like it. It is the one addition that is absolutely required to balance the dressing and make it a hit and craveable. Thanks Daniell

This is a favorite in my family. And because we have people with celiacs/non celiac gluten sensitivity, I’ve switched the pasta for a GF alternative (usually ronzoni) for family gatherings and it’s still amazing. I tweak the dressing a bit and cut just a bit of the oil out and add a touch of extra vinegar and lemon juice and the liquid from the minced garlic (if I’m using it from a jar). I also like to add some bacon bits and frozen peas. Often, I’ll switch the red onion for baby greens or just leave them out completely (I’m a bit sensitive to red onion). In short, this is a very versatile recipe. My sister-in-law and I were recently talking about switching the ingredients up entirely as her picky (and celiac) daughters do eat this when I make it and we think that this will be a good option for their lunch bags. Can’t wait to make this more!

We added cooked garbanzo beans to make this a complete meal and it was a huge hit. We didn’t use fresh garlic but instead substituted 1/4 tsp of garlic powder, and upped the oregano. Kids gobbled it up and asked for it again the next week.

I made this pasta salad for a group of around 30 high school soccer girls for a team pasta party. I had to quadruple the recipe and had some left over. One modification I made was adding a half a teaspoon of sugar to the dressing and I omitted the onions as I knew many teens wouldn’t like them. Plus, added fresh parsley and basil whisked into the dressing. Great pasta salad and will make again!
added about 1/8 cup of balsamic vinegar and white vinegar because I didn't have red wine vinegar, delicious

This is a nice pasta and the dressing is great. I would just change the noodles from penne to something a bit smaller. I used GF noodles, though, so that might have been my problem. If you use GF go with a smaller noodle. Maybe an elbow? 

Also, in keeping with the Greek theme, I think kalamata olives would have been a better option than the black. I'll switch it up next time.
Used a full cup of Kalamata olives instead of plain black olives for a flavorful kick!

I mainly followed the recipe, although I also added a bit of fresh dill for flavour, used green olives instead of black because that's what I had in the fridge, and unfortunately, didn't have any feta, so had to use Gouda cheese. The results were awesome, and I'll bet they would have been even better with feta. I'm serving the left-overs tonight, and I've fried up some chicken to add, which will make it a complete meal. I highly recommend this salad.

This is a standard greek salad mix with some pasta thrown in. Nothing bad, but nothing special. If you are in the mood for a greek salad, it is probably as good a choice as any, but I was hoping for something a bit more. I'll keep searching for something a little more exciting.
The flavors explode and you start to have a party in your bocca!
Fabulous recipe and easy to make.
Added a little extra homemade Greek dressing I have a tomato & olive hater in the family so I kept those 2 ingredients on the side and this recipe is just as tasty without
It was just what my hungry soul needed
This pasta salad is really good. I followed the recipe but I did add more feta cheese. It was a hit.
My son asks for me to make this often.
Followed directions on recipe. Took it to a gathering. Everyone loved it.
